Allowance.description:
What is left today, per capability.

Separate counters on purpose: reading a photo is a model call whether or
not a question follows it, so it must not spend a question the student has
not asked.
Allowance.title: Allowance

ExamAnswerIn.description:
One answer, with the sequence number that makes replay safe.

`client_seq` is monotonic per session on the client. The server keeps the
highest per question and ignores anything lower, so an offline queue
replaying out of order cannot overwrite a newer answer with a stale one.
ExamAnswerIn.title: ExamAnswerIn

MarkingOut.description:
Returned only once an answer is committed, and in exam mode only after
submission.
MarkingOut.title: MarkingOut

QuestionOut.description:
A question as a student sees it.

No answer key, no licence, no verification block. Their absence is the
safety property: an endpoint cannot leak a field this model does not have.
QuestionOut.title: QuestionOut

get.description:
Who is viewing, and what they may do.

Always succeeds. An anonymous viewer is a viewer: asking questions without
an account is the product's default, not a degraded mode.

Every exam format, including the key bindings its simulator needs.

The keyboard map is sent rather than compiled in, so the client hard-codes
nothing: JAMB's bindings came from JAMB's own manual and another body's
will differ.

schema.title: Response List Exams Api Catalog Exams Get

get.description:
Subjects, with honest availability.

`available` is false until a subject has enough verified content. Years
are the years that actually hold servable questions -- never padded, so a
student choosing 2019 cannot land on an empty set.

schema.title: Response List Subjects Api Catalog Subjects Get

get.description:
Topics with servable questions, and how many each has.

The count is shown because a topic with four questions is not a topic a
student should be offered a set of ten from.

schema.title: Response List Topics Api Catalog Topics  Subject Code  Get

post.description:
Start a timed sitting.

The whole paper is drawn and stored now, so the session survives going
offline: a student on an intermittent connection must not lose the exam
because the next question could not be fetched.

Autosave, including a queue replayed after being offline.

Accepts a batch so a client that has been offline flushes in one request.
Returns no marking: an exam is not marked before submission.

get.description: Score in the exam's own scale, broken down by section and topic.

post.description: Submit, and only now mark. Irreversible.

get.description:
Kept answers, rendered from their snapshot rather than from the corpus.

The snapshot is the whole point: the corpus will have moved by the time a
student revises from this, and re-rendering live would quietly change what
they saved. That is the failure this product exists to prevent, arriving
by a side door.

post.description:
Keep an answer.

Rebuilt from the stored request rather than re-answered, so saving costs
nothing and cannot produce different text from what the student read.

schema.title: Response Save To Notebook Api Notebook Post

put.description:
Save the answers, enforcing each exam's combination rules.

A broken rule is explained rather than silently rejected: the message says
which rule and why, because a student who cannot see the rule cannot fix
their choice.

post.description:
Draw a practice set from the bank.

Only servable questions, and `func.random()` rather than a fixed order so
two sets on the same topic are not the same set.

Answer one practice question, and get it marked immediately.

This is what separates practice from exam mode, and it is the only place
the two behave differently on purpose.

get.description:
Past questions with their answers and explanations visible.

Cursor-paginated and capped at 50. There is no "give me everything": the
question bank is the asset, and a bulk export endpoint would hand it over.

post.description: Ask the tutor, within one subject.
